 1.5 Million Pounds of Sausage, Hot Dogs, and More Recalled Due to Possible ‘Temperature Abuse’ 
 1.5 Million Pounds of Sausage, Hot Dogs, and More Recalled Due to Possible ‘Temperature Abuse’ 
 The recall was given the highest risk level by the USDA.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Oct 19, 2026 11:10 AM EDT Save Article Share Article FG Trade // Getty Images 2 min read Key Points 
 Kayem Foods Inc. has just recalled 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat sausage, hot dogs, and more nationwide.
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) gave the recall the highest risk level.
 Here’s a list of affected products.
 Unless you’re following a vegetarian or vegan diet, many of us have a package of sausage or hot dogs in our freezers for when we need to throw a quick meal together. But if you purchased yours recently, you may want to check the label. The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has just announced a massive recall of over 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products.
 Kayem Foods Inc. initiated the voluntary recall because the affected items “may have experienced temperature abuse during storage,” according to the USDA’s announcement . The firm discovered the issue after receiving a customer complaint about “warm product temperatures at point of delivery.” According to a release on the Kayem Foods website posted on October 16, the problem arose from “a cooling system malfunction at one of the company’s warehouses that resulted in storage temperature deviations.”
 The USDA has classified the recall at the highest risk level. Here’s everything you need to know.
 Which products are included in the recall?
 Per the USDA’s announcement, all of the meat and poultry products affected by the recall were produced by Kayem Foods Inc. between March 31, 2026, and October 7, 2026. According to the Kayem Foods release, they were stored and shipped between June 7 and October 14, 2026.
 Affected products also have the establishment numbers “EST. M/P 7839,” “EST. P 20935A,” or “EST. M 9520” on the packaging, per the USDA. The recall includes various ready-to-eat sausage, chicken, pork, bacon, and other meat products sold under the following brand names nationwide:

 More information, including a complete list of the products included in the recall and photos of the packaging, can be found in the USDA’s announcement .
 Can eating the recalled meat make you sick?
 As of right now, there are no reported illnesses associated with the recall, according to the USDA. However, there is a possibility that the meat products, which were not consistently stored at the proper temperature, could be spoiled or unsafe to eat.
 According to the USDA , leaving food in the “danger zone”—between 40°F and 140°F—for more than two hours can cause the bacteria responsible for many foodborne illnesses to grow rapidly.
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 If you have any of the recalled meat products in your fridge or freezer, the USDA urges you not to consume them and instead to throw them away or return them to where you bought them for a full refund. You can also contact Kayem Foods customer service at 800-426-6100 or info@kayem.com with any questions about the recall. If you’ve already eaten any of the recalled products and have health concerns, contact a doctor right away.
